authority.purpose: Small data-oriented design for implementing and simulating the bounded R9 controller state machine.

experiment_shape.qualification_rule: Only a matrix with 291 independently reopened VALID_PASS completions, zero other dispositions, and zero retries, replacements, or best-of is a clean matrix.

trusted: the controlled host, filesystem durability primitives, and pinned pushed Git bytes
the frozen data-only manifest, schedule, render inputs, route tuples, scorer, oracle, and reducer identities
the tiny backend adapter returning start, poll, terminal, and capture data
the offline verifier reopening immutable artifacts
controller_responsibilities: fuse one create-only attempt before dispatch
start exactly one fresh task and thread for that attempt
wait in the foreground until a typed backend terminal is observed
retain all returned poll and terminal data needed for exact raw capture
persist raw capture, deterministic score, and completion in that order
drop in-memory state and independently reopen before advance
stop dispatch permanently on controller invalidity
not_claimed: resistance to fabrication by the trusted controller
resistance to compromise or rollback by the trusted host or operating system
safety against arbitrary in-process callers invoking implementation internals
provider or model correctness beyond the exact captured boundary facts

durable_write_protocol.rule: Every controller-created final path is create-only: open with O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL and mode 0600, write the complete canonical bytes, fsync the file, close it, then fsync its parent directory. Never overwrite, truncate, delete, rename over, or repair an existing final path.
durable_write_protocol.existing_path: EEXIST is never success-by-assumption. Reopen and validate exact expected schema, bytes, bindings, and phase legality; any mismatch is CONTROLLER_INVALID.
durable_write_protocol.partial_file: A visible partial or unparsable file is permanent evidence. It is never repaired in place and makes the run CONTROLLER_INVALID.
durable_write_protocol.timestamps: Timestamps are diagnostic only. File presence plus validated content determines state.
durable_write_protocol.completion_last: Within an attempt, completion.json is created only after all six upstream attempt artifacts are durable. No later attempt artifact is permitted.
durable_write_protocol.no_mutable_cursor: There is no cursor, checkpoint, mutable counter, or progress file. The next eligible schedule row is derived from reopened completion seals and path dispositions.

durable_layout.purpose: Frozen run identity, 291-row schedule, exact route and render expectations, 291 predeclared nonces, scorer identities, and prior-series identity input.
Accepted start receipt and fresh task, thread, turn identity.
Typed terminal, typed return code, and exact poll accounting.
Exact captured output and capture-completeness classification.
Deterministic PASS, FAIL, or INVALID result bound to raw input and scorer identity.
Last attempt artifact; binds every upstream artifact by relative path, SHA-256, and byte count.
Create-only ordered or abrupt stop request.
Final matrix disposition and exact derived accounting.

constraints.nonce: exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters and equal to the value predeclared for this row

constraints: run_kind is MATRIX for this 291-row machine
expected_rows is exactly 291
schedule has exactly 291 entries with contiguous unique schedule_index values
each route has exactly 97 unique cell rows
all 291 nonces are present and unique across prior_identity_sets and this schedule
each schedule entry fixes route tuple and expected rendered SHA-256 and byte count
task_id, thread_id, and turn_id are nonempty exact opaque strings
each identity is globally fresh in its own namespace across the experiment series
the started route exactly equals expected_route

backend_rc.value_rule: integer for EXIT_CODE or SIGNAL; otherwise null

constraints: poll_count is an integer >= 1, including immediate completion
terminal_poll_index equals poll_count - 1
EXITED_ZERO iff backend_rc is {kind: EXIT_CODE, value: 0}
all common and backend identities exactly equal backend_started.json
encoding is base64
data decodes to exactly decoded_bytes and decoded_sha256
captures preserve every backend poll fragment and terminal output required by the frozen capture contract
MISSING is represented by exact empty captures, never invented content
all identities exactly equal backend_started.json
PASS or FAIL requires EXITED_ZERO and COMPLETE raw capture
nonzero, signal, timeout, transport error, protocol error, missing, partial, or malformed input deterministically yields INVALID
offline recomputation over reopened raw bytes and frozen scorer inputs must reproduce the entire result and ordered reason_codes
VALID_PASS iff score result is PASS and every eligibility predicate passes
VALID_SUBJECT_FAIL iff score result is FAIL and every controller-validity predicate passes
SEALED_CONTROLLER_INVALID iff an observed attempt can be closed with complete exact invalid evidence
the completion contains no hash of itself
a completion is a valid seal only after independent reopen validates schema, exact bindings, identities, order, and deterministic score recomputation
accounting is derived from independently reopened artifacts, never copied from mutable counters
first_decisive_row is null only for CLEAN_PASS or a stop before any decisive row

state_axes.derivation: All durable row states are derived from the longest exact create-only prefix. REOPEN_VALIDATED and ADVANCED are transient controller states and are recomputed after restart. Any artifact gap, extra attempt artifact after completion, malformed prefix, or out-of-order artifact makes the matrix INVALID.

allowed_row_transitions.guard: row is the lowest eligible schedule index; no attempt is in flight; path is ACTIVE; rendered bytes equal frozen hash and byte count
render independently reopens exact; nonce and route equal run.json; no stop is observed
one backend start only; accepted receipt supplies fresh task, thread, and turn identities
terminal and typed rc are internally consistent; every poll belongs to the exact started identity
all observed output is represented exactly; completeness has a typed value
scorer and oracle identities equal run.json; scorer consumes reopened raw bytes
all six upstream artifacts are durable and their exact path, SHA-256, and byte count are bound
fresh file descriptors reproduce schema, hashes, bytes, identities, phase order, and deterministic score
completion is VALID_PASS, or it is VALID_SUBJECT_FAIL and the path is atomically made SUBJECT_FAIL_STOPPED in derived state; completion is not invalid; no stop preempts advance
another row exists on an ACTIVE path and matrix remains ACTIVE

forbidden_transition_rule: Every row transition not listed above is forbidden. A forbidden transition, skipped eligible row, second start, identity change, attempt_ordinal other than 1, or dispatch before reopen makes the matrix permanently INVALID and permits no further backend start.

matrix_transition_rules.when: run.json and every frozen input validate before any attempt
read-only reopen finds no invalid prefix and derives the first eligible row
an abrupt or ordered stop is observed while one attempt is fused or started
a stop is observed at a boundary with no fused attempt
the sole current attempt reaches a valid reopened PASS seal; no new attempt is fused
all still-active paths finish or stop and at least one path has a reopened VALID_SUBJECT_FAIL seal, with no invalidity
all 291 rows have reopened VALID_PASS seals and all clean-matrix invariants pass
any controller-validity invariant fails; invalidity dominates subject failure and stop

subject_fail_rule.classification: A FAIL is a valid subject result only when backend terminal is EXITED_ZERO, raw capture is COMPLETE, deterministic score recomputes to FAIL, all identities and bindings validate, and completion reopens as VALID_SUBJECT_FAIL.
subject_fail_rule.effect: The failing path becomes SUBJECT_FAIL_STOPPED. No later schedule row on that path may be rendered, fused, started, retried, replaced, or selected best-of. Other ACTIVE paths may continue in global schedule order. The final matrix is VALID_SUBJECT_FAIL and receives zero clean-matrix credit.
subject_fail_rule.no_retry: The failed row already consumed its sole first attempt. It is never called again.

invalidity_and_seal_rule.unsealed_attempt: The existence of attempt.json without a valid independently reopened completion.json permanently makes the matrix CONTROLLER_INVALID_UNSEALED_ATTEMPT on restart or adjudication. No completion may be synthesized after process loss, and no backend call may be repeated.
invalidity_and_seal_rule.sealed_invalid: If the controller remains alive and exact evidence shows nonzero exit, signal, timeout, transport or protocol failure, missing/partial/malformed output, identity collision, or deterministic-score invalidity, it persists the observed raw facts, deterministic INVALID score, and SEALED_CONTROLLER_INVALID completion. The matrix then becomes CONTROLLER_INVALID_SEALED.
invalidity_and_seal_rule.priority: INVALID dominates SUBJECT_FAIL, STOPPED, and CLEAN_PASS; SUBJECT_FAIL dominates STOPPED and CLEAN_PASS; STOPPED dominates CLEAN_PASS.
invalidity_and_seal_rule.no_post_invalid_dispatch: Once any invalidity is observed or derived, backend_start_count cannot increase.

stop_and_drain.ordered_boundary_stop: Observe stop before fusing the next attempt. Persist run terminal STOPPED_ORDERED_BOUNDARY; do not render or start another row.
stop_and_drain.ordered_or_abrupt_during_attempt: Set matrix state DRAINING in memory, issue no kill, start no new attempt, continue foreground polling of the sole attempt, capture terminal and raw data, score, persist completion last, and reopen. If the completion is VALID_PASS, persist STOPPED_AFTER_DRAIN. If VALID_SUBJECT_FAIL, subject-fail precedence applies. If invalid, invalidity precedence applies.
stop_and_drain.forced_process_loss: A process loss after attempt.json exists but before a valid completion is durable is not a successful drain; reopen permanently classifies the matrix CONTROLLER_INVALID_UNSEALED_ATTEMPT.
stop_and_drain.partial_credit: Every stopped matrix is preserved but receives zero clean-matrix or qualification credit.

algorithm: Open run.json read-only and validate the full schedule and frozen identities before examining progress.
Enumerate only exact expected final paths; reject unknown attempt artifacts, duplicate indexes, gaps inside an attempted prefix, and more than one open attempt.
For each existing completion in schedule order, open all bound upstream paths using fresh file descriptors and validate exact schema, bytes, hashes, identities, and deterministic score.
Derive each path state and the matrix accounting without trusting prior in-memory counters.
If run_terminal.json exists, reopen it and require exact equality with derived disposition and accounting; make no backend call.
If any attempt.json lacks a valid completion, persist only the derived invalid run terminal if absent and make no backend call.
If a complete valid completion is the last row artifact, derive the next eligible row; never reexecute the completed row.
If only an exact complete rendered file exists for the next row and no attempt exists, reuse that exact render and proceed to the fuse; otherwise render the pending row.
If all eligible rows are terminal, persist run_terminal.json create-only and reopen it before returning.
restart_and_reopen.reopen_surface: reopen is read-only when run_terminal.json exists. It performs no backend or provider action and emits the same typed disposition and rc derived from disk.

crash_outcomes.last_durable_state: PENDING with no visible new file
crash_outcomes.restart: safe to derive and render the same row; no attempt existed
reuse only if exact frozen bytes validate; partial, corrupt, unexpected, or drifted render makes matrix INVALID before dispatch
permanent INVALID_UNSEALED_ATTEMPT; do not recover, poll, or restart the external session
permanent INVALID_UNSEALED_ATTEMPT; do not invent discarded output or terminal metadata
permanent INVALID_UNSEALED_ATTEMPT; do not resume scoring
permanent INVALID_UNSEALED_ATTEMPT; do not synthesize completion
independently reopen; if valid, derive advance without another call; if partial or invalid, matrix INVALID
transient state is discarded and deterministically re-derived from immutable files
read-only reopen; terminal matrix cannot return to ACTIVE

identity_and_dispatch_rules.predeclared_nonce: Exactly one nonce is fixed per schedule row before admission. The 291 current nonces and every nonce in prior_identity_sets are pairwise distinct.
identity_and_dispatch_rules.fresh_backend_identity: Each accepted start returns one task_id, thread_id, and turn_id. Each is pairwise distinct within its own namespace across the current run plus every prior run named by the experiment-series manifest.
identity_and_dispatch_rules.exact_binding: For a row, task_id, thread_id, turn_id, nonce, route, cell, path, and schedule index must match exactly in backend_started, backend_terminal, raw_result, score, and completion wherever that field occurs.
pre_dispatch_checks: selected row is the lowest eligible schedule index
render bytes equal the frozen expectation
attempt path does not exist before O_EXCL creation
nonce has not appeared in current or prior identity sets
identity_and_dispatch_rules.post_start_collision: If any returned task, thread, or turn identity is not fresh, preserve the exact receipt, close with SEALED_CONTROLLER_INVALID if exact closure remains possible, make the matrix INVALID, and start nothing else.

controller_return_codes.meaning: CLEAN_PASS or valid read-only reopen of CLEAN_PASS
usage or pre-admission error with zero fused attempts

equations: for every path: expected_rows = sealed_count + unsealed_attempt_count + unstarted_path_fail_stop_count + unstarted_run_stop_count + unstarted_run_invalid_count + pending_count
matrix values equal exact sums of the three path values except identity counts, which are recomputed from sets
ineligible_count = subject_fail_count + sealed_invalid_count + unsealed_attempt_count + unstarted_path_fail_stop_count + unstarted_run_stop_count + unstarted_run_invalid_count + pending_count
retry_count = sum(max(0, attempts_for_schedule_index - 1)) and must equal 0
replacement_count and best_of_count are always 0 because neither operation exists
CLEAN_PASS requires expected_rows = sealed_count = pass_count = unique_nonce_count = unique_task_count = unique_thread_count = unique_turn_count = 291 and every other count equals 0

historical_failure_constraints.fact: A started row completed externally but outer session completion metadata was discarded before seal; the row remained unsealed and the run was controller-invalid.
historical_failure_constraints.design_constraint: Terminal identity, typed rc, and poll count are captured as one durable phase before raw and score; any process loss before the final seal stays permanently invalid and is never reconstructed.

historical_failure_constraints.fact: Candidate-v21 bytes are an unfrozen zero-call development snapshot with zero empirical and qualification credit.
historical_failure_constraints.design_constraint: This design imports no candidate-v12-through-v21 runtime code and makes no retroactive evidence or readiness claim.
